title: Anthropic · Applied AI Architect, Industries
subtitle: Pre-sales architecture: discovery, take-home demo, enterprise design, values

stages.title: Application & recruiter screen
stages.tests: Written 'Why Anthropic?', motivation, role fit, views on Anthropic research, mission alignment.
stages.methodology: 90 s pitch: 10+ years customer-facing industrial equipment (CH/CN/US) → solo-built an AI platform in production → wants to bring Claude to industrial customers. Prepare views on 1–2 Anthropic papers.

stages.title: Technical deep dive & take-home
stages.tests: Depth on LLM systems you built; a ~3–4 h take-home building a small Claude app for a fictional customer, then a live demo/presentation.
stages.methodology: Presentation: customer problem & success criteria → architecture diagram → prompt & tool design → evals with numbers → failure modes & guardrails → cost/latency (caching, batches, model choice) → next steps. State assumptions.

stages.title: Customer discovery role-play
stages.tests: Discovery, listening, objection handling, not over-promising with a skeptical stakeholder.
stages.methodology: Agenda → business context & KPIs → current process & quantified pain → data (sources, sensitivity, residency) → constraints (security, ZDR, procurement, integration) → success criteria & eval ownership → stakeholders & decision process → scoped pilot → written recap.

stages.title: Enterprise solution design
stages.tests: Enterprise LLM deployments: secure integration with legacy systems, knowledge retrieval with RBAC, evaluation harnesses, safety and deployment risk.
stages.methodology: Requirements → architecture (workflow vs agent, model tiering, RAG with citations, tools/MCP) → evals → guardrails → human checkpoints → security (RBAC, audit, retention) → rollout (pilot → shadow → staged).

stages.title: Values & mission
stages.tests: Mission alignment and safety reasoning; several guides call it the round with many rejections.
stages.methodology: STAR stories: telling a customer 'no/not yet' for safety or quality, an ambiguous ethical tradeoff, admitting and fixing a mistake — each connected to the RSP and Core Views.
